1.  Minutes
  Although the live recording is the official record of public meetings, actions are prepared

  Recommended Action

2.  Classification and Compensation Study Request for Proposal

GENERAL BUSINESS
3.  Appointing a Mayor Pro-Tern
  The City Clerk will call for nominations for Mayor Pro Tern. If there is more than one
  nomination, voting for those nominated will be conducted. The person receiving the most
  votes will be declared the Mayor Pro Tern.
  Recommended Action
  Nominate and vote on a member of the City Council to serve as the Mayor Pro Tern.

4.  Audit Committee
  There are two members of City Council that sit on the audit committee. Their job is to
  review all warrants that go before the City Council for approval.
  Recommended Action
  Appoint two members of the City Council to serve as the Audit Committee.

5.  Award Contract for Joe Machado Field (JMF) Concession Stand
  In February, 2024 City Council authorized City Staff to issue a request for proposals (RFP)
  for the concessions at Joe Machado Field (JMF). The deadline to submit proposals was
  1 p.m. on Wednesday, April 1, 2024. The City received four proposals by the stated
  deadline.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute a lease agreement with Santiago
  Bryan-Zwick dba Avalon Smokehouse, Inc. for the concession at Joe Machado Field.

6.  Wrigley Road Traffic Safety Improvements
  Wrigley Road, the steep "high road" linking Clemente Avenue to Pebbly Beach Road, is
  comprised of four curves - Catalina Pet Cemetery, 333 Wrigley Road, Buena Vista Point
  and 3 Palms. These four roadway curves do not include any striping or supplementary
  warning signage to notify drivers of the curving inclined condition.
  Recommended Action
  Approve the plan as presented for modifications and striping along Wrigley Road in the
  space designated including five curves between the Pet Cemetery and Buena Vista
  Point.
ADJOURN

on Friday, April 12, 2024 on the City's website www.cityofavalon.com/agendacenter, and at City
Hall, 410 Avalon Canyon Road.

Devin Elise Hart, Management Analyst

SUBJECT:  Classification and Compensation Study Request for
  Proposal

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize City staff to publish a request for proposals
(RFP) for consultant services to conduct a Classification and Compensation Study.

REPORT SUMMARY:  The City of Avalon last completed a classification and
compensation study in 2015. Due to emergency MOU changes in 2020, a classification
and compensation study was not completed at that time due to significant financial crisis.

In the current 2022-2025 MOUs for the SEIU Avalon Municipal Employees and SEIU
Avalon Harbor Employees MOU5 state the City and (3) members selected by the union
will work together with the consultant selection process and meet to mutually decide how
to apply the findings of a City Classification and Compensation Study.

Therefore, it is recommended to publish an RFP for a City Classification and
Compensation Study, inclusive of all active City job classifications. The requested
services will including benchmarking and survey design, total compensation analysis,
market and competitiveness analysis, findings, and a final report.

If approved, City staff will publish a standard template RFP on Tuesday, April 30, 2024
with a tentative closing date of Tuesday June 4, 2024. Received proposals will be
reviewed by the panel, the top scoring consultants invited to present, and a
recommendation to City Council for a tentative award on July 16, 2024 (after adoption of
the FY24/25 budget).

FISCAL IMPACTS: City staff are requesting $60,000 to hire a consultant to complete the
survey within the proposed FY24/25 operating budget. An updated Classification and
Compensation Study will assist the City in determining competitive wages.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Fiscal and organizational stability.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City may
not meet stated deadline to revise classification structures, policies and procedures.
 FOLLOW UP ACTION: Publish a Classification and Compensation Study RFP and
complete the City procurement process.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: The item was properly listed on the
posted agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.

SUBJECT:  Award Contract for Joe Machado Field (JMF) Concession Stand

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute a lease
agreement with Santiago Bryan-Zwick dba Avalon Smokehouse, Inc. for the concession at Joe
Machado Field.

REPORT SUMMARY: On February 6, 2024 City Council authorized City Staff to issue a
request for proposals (RFP) for the concessions at Joe Machado Field (JMF). The RFP was
published on February 26, 2024. City Staff conducted a non-mandatory pre-proposal meeting
and walk through the lease space on March 20, 2024; a total of 12 people representing four
potential respondents attended.

The deadline to submit proposals was 1 p.m. on Wednesday, April 1, 2024. The City received
four proposals by the stated deadline: (in alphabetical order)
  -  Santiago Bryan-Zwick dba Avalon Smokehouse, Inc.
  -  Christina Grain dba Huaraches La Dona
  -  Julio Marquez
  -  Maria Dinazar Octavo

City Staff evaluated proposals based on the best interests of the City and the following criteria,
as outlined in the RFP:
  -  The firm has no conflict of interest with regard to any other work performed by the firm
  for the City.
  -  Clarity and conformance of proposal to RFP.
  -  Content of the proposal.
  -  Proposer’s experience and performance.
  -  Team members’ experience and performance.

In terms of considering “content of the proposals,” City Staff considered the following elements:
  1. Food/Menu.
  2. Proposer’s Overall Restaurant Business Experience. Including, but not limited to, the
  qualifications and experience of business’s personnel who will be overseeing
  services and managing operations.
  3. MarketingNision. How the vendor plans to increase their market share for the future.

Of the four proposals received, three conformed to the format outlined in the RFP and provided
all of the information requested; however, based on the “content of the proposal” criteria, one
proposer stood out significantly Santiago Bryan-Zwick dba Avalon Smokehouse, Inc.
  -
 The proposal provided by Santiago Bryan-Zwick dba Avalon Smokehouse, Inc. included a fully
formed and thoughtful menu, commitment to investments in the facility, and plans for
partnership and growth in the community. Additionally, the principle, Santiago Bryan-Zwick,
has significant experience in the restaurant business in Avalon.

Staff recommends awarding the contract for JMF Concessions to Santiago Bryan-Zwick dba
Avalon Smokehouse, Inc.

Staff recommend City Council authorize the City Manager to enter into negotiations with
Santiago Bryan-Zwick dba Avalon Smokehouse, Inc. to establish the following terms for
concession operations:
  • Continuous year-round operation of the concession stand;
  • Require the concession stand to be open for all events at JMF, including recreational
  activities, school sports events, contracted league events, etc.;
  • Enter  an  approximate  2  year  agreement  with  lessee,  expiring  on
  April 30, 2025;
  • Before the initial term of operation expires, City Staff will conduct an internal review of
  operations. In the event both parties are satisfied and the Lessee is meeting the
  minimum requirements of the lease agreement allow for an additional 3-year term;
  • Maintain insurance coverage consistent with the requirements outlined by the AMC;
  • Comply with all aspects of the AMC, including the City’s Fats, Oil, Grease (“FOG”)
  ordinance, Styrofoam, plastic straw and plastic bag ban ordinance, etc.;
  • Establish an initial lease rate of $2 per square foot for the first six months, and up to the
  first year of operations. After six months, the City Manager may consider an increase
  the lease rate to the standard $4 per square foot subject to annual CPI. The available
  lease space is comprised of 279 square feet of interior space and 121 square feet of
  outdoor space previously used to store a food vendor cart. The initial monthly rental
  rate of just the interior space is approximately $558 and $1,116 after six months of
  operation. Including the outdoor storage space, the initial monthly lease rate would be
  $800 and $1,600 after six months of operation.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Provide food service at Joe Machado Field for community gatherings
including but not limited to: City recreation and school athletic games; community special
events, and private gatherings were food is being served.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Lease revenue.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: Food services will not
be provided and no monthly rent be collected at Joe Machado Field for the snack bar services.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Implement City Council direction.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: Pursuant to the Brown Act.

My management approach to accomplish a successful service to the city is to be hands on. I

will be teaching everyone on my team my ways of food prep and making all the rubs and

sauces personally. My Equipment is top of the line and consistent. It’s programmed to run

the preset program sequence (cooking meat at the same temperature for a preset length

of time then turns into a hold holding cabinet). This ensures that the food is not

overcooked hut cooked to perfection while holding at a food safe temperature allowing the

fat to render even more. I upgraded the smoker to have this program in order to maintain

a consistent cook in case another cook puts the meat into the smoker other than myself. It

also has a lockbox over the control panel to ensure only staff has access to controls. All

these steps are being taken to accomplish the work load with minimal staff yet producing

enough meat in order to stock Virgies for a busy weekend and enough for an event if one is

SUBJECT:  Wrigley Road Traffic Safety Improvements

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Approve the plan as presented for modifications and striping
along Wrigley Road in the space designated including four curves between the Pet Cemetery
and Buena Vista Point.

REPORT SUMMARY: Wrigley Road, the steep “high road” linking Clemente Avenue to Pebbly
Beach Road, is comprised of four curves Catalina Pet Cemetery, 333 Wrigley Road, Buena
  —

Vista Point and 3 Palms. These four roadway curves do not include any striping or
supplementary warning signage to notify drivers of the curving inclined condition.

Wrigley Road is frequently used by visitors and is a main arterial road when Pebbly Beach
Road is closed.

Working cooperatively with W-Trans, California Traffic Engineering Consultants, City Staff
developed recommendations based on direction from the California Manual on Uniform Traffic
Control Devices (MUTCD) as well as engineering judgement, to make recommendations to
enhance the safety of the road.

  1. The City should stripe a yellow centerline through the curve to provide an 11-foot inside
  lane and 10-foot outside lane, as well as white edge line separating a 6-foot parking
  pullout where there is 27 feet of width in front of the Pet Cemetery. The red “No Parking”
  edge line striping should be removed on the Pet Cemetery side of the road.

  2. The City should install a W-1 1 Hairpin Curve warning sign in the downhill direction
  placed 100 feet in advance of the start of the curve. While the City’s speed limit in
  Avalon is 20 mph, curve conditions and engineering judgement indicate that a more
  appropriate speed through the curve is 10 mph. The W-1 1 sign is justified based on the
  following excerpt from the MUTCD: “If the curve has a change in horizontal alignment of
  135 degrees or more, the Hairpin Curve (Wi-il) sign may be used instead of a Curve
  or Turn sign.”

  3. The City should install a W13-1P Advisory Speed plaque with the Wi-li Hairpin Curve
  warning sign showing a speed of 10 mph. The MUTCD recommends that: “The advisory
  speed shall be determined by an engineering study that follows established engineering
  practices.” In this case, engineering judgement was used.
   4. The City should consider if similar measures are appropriate at the other three curves
  on Wrigley Road including 333 Wrigley Road, Buena Vista Point and 3 Palms.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Traffic safety.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Undetermined.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING  RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  No  safety
improvements will be made to the Wrigley

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Implement City Council direction.
